summary.headline: Veranda Q2 FY27 continuing-business revenue rose 17% YoY to ₹51 crore and EBITDA 28% to ₹12.7 crore after commerce demerger.
summary.overview: Veranda reported Q2 FY27 results on a continuing-business basis, with the commerce vertical (J.K. Shaw Commerce Education) demerged effective 1 September 2026 and its profit shown as discontinued operations. Revenue for the quarter was ₹51 crore (up 17% YoY) and reported EBITDA was ₹12.7 crore (margin 25% vs 23% in Q1), while finance costs fell 58% YoY to ₹4.8 crore. Reported PAT was ₹13.4 crore versus a loss of ₹12.8 crore a year earlier, but this includes a one-time non-operational exceptional gain of ₹1,047 crore from fair valuation of the demerged business. Management reaffirmed FY27 continuing-business guidance of ₹175 crore revenue, ₹46 crore EBITDA and ₹32 crore PAT.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 31% YoY in H1 on enrolment and admission traction; network of over 40 centres across South India covering UPSC, SSC, banking, TNPSC and state exams. Karnataka expansion started with a Mysore centre; plan is 4 centres this year and 4 next year.

segments.name: Academic / K-12 and managed schools
segments.commentary: Revenue declined slightly YoY in Q2, which management attributed to book issuance timing (heavier in Q1). Six managed schools with over 5,400 students; target of 30+ schools over the next few years. Preschool entry planned under the Veranda's Proust name.

segments.name: SNBA Veranda (associate, ~40% stake)
segments.commentary: Online and campus-based university partner business with three US online universities, one EU online university, a physical campus in Lyon and a Dubai campus planned. Management hinted at options that could lift stake value over the next couple of quarters, with listing targeted in the 'near future'.

guidance_outlook: FY27 continuing-business guidance reaffirmed: revenue ₹175 crore, EBITDA ₹46 crore, PAT ₹32 crore.
Commerce business PAT guidance of ₹110 crore for full FY27 (₹53 crore achieved in the 5 months to demerger); management expects ~₹110 crore or more for the full year.
Long-term aspiration of roughly ₹600 crore revenue in five years across government test prep and schools; EBITDA margin target of ₹120-140 crore (figure as stated on call, unclear).
Karnataka centres expected to reach EBITDA of about ₹20-25 crore in 4-5 years, in line with Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
Management views current EBITDA margins as sustainable despite new centre costs, citing new programmes offsetting start-up costs.
Dividend not ruled out but no commitment; cash to be reinvested in government test prep and managed schools for now.
capex_capacity: Karnataka: first centre opened in Mysore two days before the call; plan of 4 centres in FY27 and 4 in FY28.
Investment per centre expected at ₹30-35 lakh including interiors and rental deposit.
Managed schools: six schools, no new school added in the last two years apart from one international school; new curriculum introduced across Classes 1-12 in the last 6-7 months.
Capacity utilisation rising in existing centres; student growth achieved without new capacity additions.
demand_pricing: Fee increases of about 7-10% YoY contribute to revenue growth; cost inflation about 4% per year.
Junior IAS and new PSE/subscription offerings drove significant student count growth.
Private equity interest in K-12 is rising; management expects it to raise valuations and push smaller schools toward aggregation under Veranda's brand.
Management described Karnataka state competitive exam market as a 30-35% growth opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is academic revenue flat or declining while government test prep grows 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the admission and book-issuance season, so Q1 sales were higher; H1 vs H1 academic revenue grew 12% from ₹17 crore to ₹19 crore, and EBITDA rose from ₹11 crore to ₹20 crore (as stated on call).

qa_highlights.question: Why did government test prep EBITDA grow 29% against 31% revenue growth, and is the current margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were annual fee hikes of 7-10%, higher capacity utilisation of existing centres, and new programmes such as Junior IAS; management called current EBITDA margins sustainable, with new-centre costs offset by new programmes.

qa_highlights.question: How many schools were added in the last three years, and what is the expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost no new schools were added after the first post-acquisition year, when promoters were phased out and systems stabilised; growth focus is now on managed schools via partnerships with existing school owners and preschool entry.

qa_highlights.question: How should the economics of the Karnataka expansion be evaluated, including capex per centre?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ₹30-35 lakh per centre including interiors and rental deposit, with a 4-5 year path to Tamil Nadu/Kerala-level EBITDA of ₹20-25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a fair value gain recognised instead of common-control accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ind AS treatment applies because no single shareholder holds more than 51%, so the demerger is accounted for at fair value rather than as a common-control transaction.

qa_highlights.question: Will the dividend be paid, and what is the book value?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend to be considered by the commerce entity's board in the future; non-commerce cash flows will be reinvested. Book value of the parent cited as about ₹54 per share post-demerger (as stated on call).

risks_watch: Exceptional gain of ₹1,047 crore inflates reported PAT; underlying profitability is much lower and the one-off should be stripped out.
Post-demerger share price weakness; the parent's trading level relative to book value is a shareholder concern raised on the call.
Academic segment revenue flat in Q2 due to book-issuance timing; watch Q3/Q4 for recovery.
Karnataka ramp-up and new managed school additions will add start-up costs that may pressure margins.
Commerce demerger listing (J.K. Shaw Commerce Education) expected within days; watch for listing price and investor presentation.
Timing and terms of SNBA Veranda options and possible listing; management said results would come in the next couple of quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with management stressing operating leverage and deleveraging. Evasive on dividends, timing of new school additions, and the valuation gap, deferring to future quarters and the listing. Several answers on the SNBA stake and the commerce listing were deliberately vague ('too early to comment').

growth.why: Reaffirmed FY27 continuing guidance of ₹175 cr revenue (brief says reaffirmed, though the quote tags it as a cut, so the direction is unclear) and ₹46 cr EBITDA; delivery backed by 7-10% fee hikes, government test prep growth of 31% in H1, and Karnataka centres (1 of 4 open, 4 more in FY28), with no firm capacity numbers for FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA margin rose to 25% in Q2 from 23% in Q1, and management called current margins sustainable with new programmes offsetting Karnataka start-up costs, though 4% cost inflation against 7-10% fee hikes is the driver.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: First Karnataka centre (Mysore) opened two days before the call, with 4 more planned in FY27 and 4 in FY28 at ₹30-35 lakh each; managed schools to scale from 6 to 30+ over several years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Government test prep revenue grew 31% YoY in H1 on enrolment traction, with higher utilisation of existing centres and Junior IAS adding students; academic revenue recovery depends on Q3/Q4 book issuance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Karnataka roll-out (₹30-35 lakh per centre) is already committed, but no new group-level capex was guided; utilisation is rising without new capacity, not explicitly quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 continuing guidance of ₹175 crore revenue, ₹46 crore EBITDA and ₹32 crore PAT was only reaffirmed; H1 revenue of ₹104 crore implies a H2 run-rate of ₹71 crore needed, leaving little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue of ₹104 crore leaves ₹71 crore for H2 to hit ₹175 crore, and academic revenue was flat in Q2 with start-up costs from new centres and schools ahead.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Preschool entry under the Proust name is planned, and Junior IAS plus new PSE/subscription offerings already drove student growth; no launch date given.

rows.label: SNBA Veranda stake value unlock / listing
rows.why: Management hinted at options that could lift the ~40% SNBA stake value over the next couple of quarters, with listing targeted in the 'near future', but terms were kept vague.

rows.label: Commerce demerger listing (J.K. Shaw Commerce Education)
rows.why: Demerger effective 1 September 2026 with listing expected within days; commerce PAT of ₹53 crore in 5 months to demerger against ₹110 crore FY27 guidance.

rows.label: Annual fee hikes in test prep
rows.why: Fee increases of about 7-10% YoY are contributing to revenue growth, against cost inflation of about 4% per year.
